- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% if recent price is trending down.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 2–3 days to avoid overcorrection.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to reflect this; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–7 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 3–5 day moving average of recent 18-day history as baseline for adjustment.  
- If true outcome is consistently higher than model (especially in 30d horizon), model may be underestimating long-term trend; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment is bullish and price is rising.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33), model often fails to capture sentiment drift; use sentiment average over last 5 days to adjust forecast direction.
